extracted.intended_audience: applicants and licensees for 220-222 MHz spectrum (private radio operators, frequency coordinators, and counsel preparing license applications)
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and operational standards governing assignment, construction, operation, reporting, and technical limits for applicants and licensees in the 220-222 MHz band.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing order for pending applications
rubrics_metrics.description: All applications in pending status will be processed in the order in which they are received, determined by the date on which the application was received by the Commission in its Gettysburg, Pennsylvania Office (or the address set forth at § 0.401(b) for applications requiring the fees established by Part 1, Subpart G of this chapter), except as otherwise provided in this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes first-in-first-out processing unless another provision alters order. Applications accepted for filing will then be reviewed to determine whether they can be granted. An application which is dismissed will lose its place in the processing line. If returned for correction and resubmitted and received within 60 days from return it will retain its place; otherwise it will lose its place.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance and review
rubrics_metrics.description: Each application that is accepted for filing will then be reviewed to determine whether it can be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequencies will be assigned by the Commission pursuant to the provisions of § 90.723. Acceptance for filing does not guarantee grant — subject to substantive review and assignment rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place retention on resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application is returned for correction and resubmitted and received by the Commission within 60 days from the date on which it was returned to the applicant, it will retain its place in the processing line. If it is not received within 60 days, it will lose its place in the processing line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely resubmission (≤60 days) preserves filing priority; late resubmission forfeits priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry criteria — geographic construction certification
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must certify that, within ten years of receiving a license, they will construct a minimum of one base station in at least 70 of the top 100 MSAs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is specifically for the two blocks of ten and six blocks of five contiguous channels set aside for exclusive nationwide non-Government assignments (§ 90.717). Certification is a required part of entry eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry criteria — meet construction requirements of § 90.725
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must certify that they will meet the construction requirements set forth in § 90.725.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant acknowledges adherence to the benchmark schedule and consequences for non-compliance specified in § 90.725.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry criteria — ten-year schedule and cost estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must submit a ten year schedule detailing plans for construction of the proposed system as well as an itemized estimate of the cost of constructing and operating the system during the ten year term of the initial license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule must include milestones and itemized cost estimates to demonstrate feasibility of the nationwide system over the license term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry criteria — financial resources showing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must demonstrate that they have sufficient financial resources to construct and operate the proposed system for the initial ten year term of license; i.e., that they have net current assets sufficient to cover estimated costs or a firm financial commitment sufficient to cover estimated costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two alternative showings permitted: demonstration of internal net current assets or a firm financial commitment from a lender/sponsor. Applicant must substantiate either path with documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial statements when relying on internal resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants relying on personal or internal resources must submit financial statements certified within one year of the date of the application showing net current assets sufficient to meet estimated construction and operating costs, and a balance sheet dated no more than sixty days before the date of the application showing continued availability; the applicant or an officer must attest to validity of the unaudited balance sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires recent certified financials and a very recent balance sheet (≤60 days). Attestation by applicant/officer is mandatory for unaudited balance sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Firm financial commitment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants submitting evidence of a firm financial commitment must obtain the commitment from a bona fide commercially acceptable source (e.g., bank, savings and loan, recognized financial institution, financial arm of capital equipment supplier, or investment banking house). If the lender is a non-conventional source, the lender must demonstrate it has funds available to cover total commitments made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The commitment must be supported by a lender statement addressing four specific points (see next metric). Non-traditional lenders face additional scrutiny to show actual availability of funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lender commitment statements (four elements)
rubrics_metrics.description: The lender's commitment shall contain a statement that the lender: (1) has examined the financial condition of the applicant and determined applicant is creditworthy; (2) has examined the financial viability of the proposed system; (3) is willing to provide a sum sufficient to cover realistic and prudent estimated costs for the initial term; and (4) is willing to enter into the commitment solely on the basis of the lender's relationship with the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each element must be explicitly addressed in the lender's commitment. Examination of audited financials where applicable should be documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequencies assigned in pairs and channel listing
rubrics_metrics.description: Frequencies shall be assigned in pairs, with base station frequencies taken from the 220-221 MHz band and corresponding mobile and control station frequencies 1 MHz higher in the 221-222 MHz band. Only the lower half of the frequency pair(s) is listed in the table.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should request channel pairs consistent with the table of 220-222 MHz channel designations; assignments will follow the paired scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Channel block designations and eligibility (nationwide non-commercial)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two blocks of ten and six blocks of five contiguous channels have been set aside for exclusive assignments for non-Government use on a nationwide basis. Channels 21-30 and 51-60 are 10-channel blocks available to applicants eligible in all part 90 services only for nationwide non-commercial systems for voice and/or data use. Channels 81-85 and 86-90 are 5-channel blocks available to applicants eligible in all part 90 services only for nationwide non-commercial systems for voice and/or data use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These blocks are restricted to nationwide non-commercial systems (internal use). Applicants must be eligible in all part 90 services to qualify for these nationwide non-commercial blocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of non-commercial and data
rubrics_metrics.description: The term 'non-commercial system' is defined as a system that will be used only for a licensee's internal use. The term 'data' includes the transmission of text, control codes, and other information typical of machine-to-machine communications. Digitized voice signals are considered data signals under this subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies permitted use and what counts as data; digitized voice treated as data for assignment and operational rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Channel blocks for commercial and Government use
rubrics_metrics.description: Channels 141-145, 146-150, 151-155, and 156-160 are 5-channel blocks available to non-Government applicants only for nationwide commercial systems for voice and/or data use. Channels 111-115 and 116-120 are 5-channel blocks available for Government nationwide use only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different blocks are reserved depending on commercial vs Government and eligibility; applicants must request appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability and transitional limitations for channels 161-200
rubrics_metrics.description: Channels 161-200 are available to both Government and non-Government applicants. Non-Government access to these channels will be limited to applicants eligible in all part 90 services for non-commercial operations until March 31, 1995, after which commercial operations to serve part 90 eligibles and the Government may be authorized. Channels 161-170 available for voice and data; Channels 171-200 assigned only for data systems and set aside for data-only operations until March 31, 2000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transitional calendar restrictions govern when channels may be used commercially or for voice; applicants must observe date-based availability constraints and data-only designations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application content — specify number and intended use
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications shall specify the number of frequencies requested and whether intended use is for 5 or 10-channel nationwide systems, commercial or non-commercial use, 5-channel trunked systems, individual data/voice use, or individual data only use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precise statement of requested channels and intended service type is required on the application to guide assignment decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment limits — number justified and five-channel maximum
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants will be assigned only the number of channels justified to meet their requirements. Except for the 10-channel nationwide assignments, the maximum number of frequencies that will be assigned to an applicant at any one time is five.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must justify channel quantity; default cap is five channels unless qualifying for a 10-channel nationwide block.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sub-band separation of base station receivers and transmitters
rubrics_metrics.description: Base stations utilizing channels from Sub-band A (220.000-220.300 MHz) will be separated from base stations utilizing channels from Sub-Band B (220.700-221.000 MHz) by specified geographic separation distances depending on effective radiated power. Transmitter peak envelope power shall be used to determine effective radiated power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A table (not fully reproduced here) prescribes separation distances (km) corresponding to ERP levels (e.g., 0.5W, 5W, 10W, 20W, etc.). Applicants must justify power levels requested and use peak envelope power to compute ERP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobile station transmission authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: A mobile station is authorized to transmit on any frequency assigned to its associated base station.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mobile stations inherit authorization for frequencies assigned to their base station; operational conformity required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-channel separation (non-nationwide)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for nationwide assignments, the separation of co-channel systems will be 120 kilometers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and coordinators must observe 120 km protection spacing for co-channel operations unless handling nationwide assignments subject to different rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction requirements for nationwide authorizations (benchmarks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensees granted nationwide authorizations must construct base stations in the markets designated in the application as follows: (1) In at least 10% of the markets designated within two years of licensing, (2) at least 40% within four years, (3) at least 70% within six years, and (4) in all designated markets within ten years of licensing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Progress toward nationwide construction is benchmarked by percentage of markets and firm deadlines; licensees must file progress reports at conclusion of each period per § 90.725(a)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for missing construction benchmarks (2- & 4-year)
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensees not meeting the two and four year criteria shall lose the entire authorization, but will be permitted a six month period to convert the system to non-nationwide channels, if such channels are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure at early benchmarks is harsh (loss of entire authorization) but conversion window provided if channels exist; timely monitoring and reporting critical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for missing construction benchmarks (6- & 10-year)
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensees not meeting the six and ten year criteria shall lose the authorizations for the facilities not constructed, but will retain exclusivity for its constructed facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial loss of authorization applies for later benchmark failures; constructed facilities remain exclusive, unconstructed facilities are forfeited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Progress reporting for construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Progress reports will be filed at the conclusion of each of the above periods to inform the Commission of the status of the system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory filings at each benchmark completion are required to document compliance; see § 90.725(a)(4) and § 90.737(a) for filing instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment/transfer condition — 40% construction before transfer
rubrics_metrics.description: Licenses for nationwide systems may be assigned or transferred only after the licensee has constructed at least 40% of the proposed system. The assignee or transferee of a nationwide system is subject to the construction benchmarks and reporting requirements in paragraph (a). The assignee or transferee is not subject to the entry criteria described in § 90.713.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignment/transfer is contingent on meeting a 40% construction threshold; new owner must comply with ongoing benchmarks and reports but not entry-stage certification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction requirement for non-nationwide systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensees authorized non-nationwide systems will be permitted twelve months to construct the system. Authorizations for systems not constructed within twelve months from the date of grant will cancel automatically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-nationwide systems have a strict 12-month build deadline; automatic cancellation if not completed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extended implementation schedules (up to 3 years) — justification criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for nationwide and commercial systems, a period of up to three years may be authorized for constructing and placing a system in operation if the applicant submits justification that includes reasons for requiring an extended construction period, the construction schedule (with milestones), and shows one of: (1) large fleet/multi-year planning/funding cycle; (2) purpose/size/complexity requiring >12 months; (3) part of coordinated area-wide system requiring >12 months; or (4) applicant is a local governmental agency demonstrating government, funding, and purchasing the proposed system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extended schedules are exceptional and must be supported with a milestones-based schedule and substantive reasons aligned with the enumerated categories. Not available for nationwide or commercial systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditioning and consequences for extended schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorizations under this section are conditioned upon the licensee’s compliance with the submitted extended implementation schedule. Failure to meet the schedule will result in loss of authorizations for facilities not constructed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant of extension imposes binding schedule obligations; non-compliance leads to loss of unconstructed authorizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations of power and antenna height (ERP vs HAAT)
rubrics_metrics.description: The permissible effective radiated power (ERP) with respect to antenna heights shall be determined from the Table. These are maximum values and applicants are required to justify power levels requested. Transmitter peak envelope power shall be used to determine effective radiated power. The maximum permissible ERP for mobile units is 20 watts. Portable units are considered as mobile units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must compute ERP using peak envelope power and justify any requested ERP; HAAT-to-ERP table prescribes maximum ERP by height band (e.g., Up to 90 m = 200 W; 90-120 m = 100 W; ... Above 275 m = 20 W). Mobile/portable units capped at 20 W ERP.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on operational-fixed stations
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for control stations, operational-fixed stations will not be authorized in the 220-222 MHz band. Licensees may utilize their authorized frequencies for fixed signaling in accordance with § 90.235 of this part. Control stations associated with one or more mobile relay stations will be authorized only on the assigned frequency of the associated mobile station. Use of a mobile service frequency by a control station of a mobile relay system is subject to the condition that harmful interference shall not be caused to stations of licensees authorized to use the frequency for mobile service communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational-fixed service is generally prohibited; limited fixed signaling allowed per § 90.235. Control stations must use assigned mobile frequencies and avoid causing harmful interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible operations — service types and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems authorized in the 220-222 MHz band may be used: (1) Only for base/mobile and mobile relay transmission on a primary basis, and fixed voice and signaling transmissions on a secondary basis. Paging operations are not permitted in this band. (2) Only by persons who are eligible for facilities under either this subpart or in the radio services included in subparts B, C, D, or E of this part. (3) Only for the transmission of messages or signals permitted in the services in which the licensees are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational use is constrained by primary/secondary service categorization, eligibility of the user, and message/signal permissibility. Paging explicitly prohibited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple emissions in authorized contiguous channels
rubrics_metrics.description: When two or more contiguous channels are authorized to a single licensee (up to a ten channel nationwide block), more than a single emission may be utilized within the authorized bandwidth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensee may employ multiple emission types within the assigned contiguous bandwidth; frequency coordination and technical compliance required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Station identification rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for nationwide and trunked systems authorized in the 220-222 MHz band, station identification is required pursuant to § 90.425. Systems authorized on nationwide frequencies pursuant to this subpart do not require station identification. Trunked systems shall employ an automatic device to transmit the call sign of the base station at 30 minute intervals on the lowest frequency in the base station trunked group; if that frequency is in use, identification may be made at termination of the communication in progress. Identification may be by voice or International Morse Code. If transmitted in Morse Code it must be at a rate between 15 to 20 words per minute, by tone modulation with tone frequency 800–1000 Hz.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trunked systems have automatic 30-minute ID requirement on lowest assigned trunked frequency; nationwide systems are exempt; Morse code ID has specified speed and tone constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Licensees of nationwide systems must file progress reports pursuant to § 90.725(a)(4). Licensees offering service on a commercial basis must maintain records of the names and addresses of each customer and dates service commenced and terminated and make these available to the Commission upon request; such licensees must report at renewal the number of mobile units being served. Non-commercial trunked system licensees must report at renewal the number of mobile units being served. Except for licensees of nationwide systems, all licensees must report whether construction of the facility has been completed within 12 months of the date of grant of their license. All reports must be filed with the Land Mobile Branch, Licensing Division, Private Radio Bureau, Gettysburg, PA 17326.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific recordkeeping and reporting obligations differ by system type; renewal reports must include counts of mobile units for commercial and non-commercial trunked licensees. Timely filings to the specified office are mandatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number of systems authorized in an area and protest limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be no limit on the number of systems authorized to operate in any one given area except that imposed by frequency assignment limitations. No person shall have a right to protest any application or grant on grounds other than violation of any of the provisions of this subpart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frequency assignment constraints (technical/spacing) rather than numerical caps limit systems. Protest rights are limited to asserted violations of the subpart provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special licensing requirements for commercial systems — end user licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: End users on commercial systems must be licensed for any associated control points, control stations, and mobile units and only licensed end users are authorized to use those systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial system operators must ensure end users hold proper licenses for associated equipment and only licensed end users may operate on commercial systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary permit to operate under an authorized facility
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant for a license to utilize an already authorized facility may operate its station(s) for a period of up to 180 days under a temporary permit evidenced by a properly executed certification of FCC Form 572 after filing a formal application for station license, provided the antenna(s) employed by the control station(s) is(are) 6.1 meters or less above ground or 6.1 meters or less above a man-made structure other than an antenna tower to which it is affixed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporary operation (≤180 days) is conditional on filing a formal application and meeting antenna height limits (≤6.1 m above ground or ≤6.1 m above certain man-made structures). Form 572 certification required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of permissible product/service descriptions (from Commerce excerpt)
rubrics_metrics.description: For determinations concerning imports (example: mechanical transfer presses), scope language is dispositive and HTS/TSUSA numbers are provided for convenience; merchandise definitions may be clarified (e.g., 'designed as an integral part of the press') based on comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When regulatory notices include product-scope content, the written description controls classification and scope; tariff numbers are auxiliary. Clarifications may be added in the final determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign market value methodology (example guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: When home-market comparisons are not reasonable, constructed value (CV) may be used to calculate foreign market value; CV includes materials, fabrication, general expenses, profit, and packing; statutory minima (e.g., 8% profit, 10% general expenses floor) apply; adjustments for imputed credit costs and differences in circumstances of sale should be made in accordance with regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an example of evidentiary and valuation standards appearing elsewhere in the chunk (pertaining to antidumping investigations). It shows how agencies specify calculation components, statutory minima, and required adjustments when selecting valuation bases.
